title: Continuing a chapter by voice
description: Adding a new dictation to the right part of the manuscript while keeping the text linked to the source audio.

blocks.text: The author opens the chapter they need and adds a new dictation where they left off. The previous text stays available, and the new fragment can be listened to, corrected and accepted into the manuscript.

quote.text: If you want to write an article or a book, there is no way that you can end one dictating session and then open the transcription up to add additional text by dictating it

blocks.text: To begin with, a structure of chapters and a controlled way of adding text to the end of the chosen part is enough. It matters to tell a new recording apart from a version already edited, so that transcribing again does not overwrite the author’s work.
Dictation as part of the manuscript

The quote below describes outright that a session cannot be continued. That is a more concrete basis for the idea than general praise for daily dictation; a full book editor is worth adding only if the existing way of moving the text really gets in the way of the work.
